- Overestimate prices when sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.75) — model tends to overshoot early in the horizon.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.3) — model fails to capture downward momentum.
- Model consistently overreacts to recent spikes; reduce forecast peak values by 5–10% after a price spike.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show high sentiment + high price, model overweights momentum; dampen forecast by 2–5% per day.
- Forecast horizon 30d: model often misses early downward corrections — adjust downward by 1–3% for days 1–7 if sentiment turns negative.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.0–0.5), model tends to overpredict — apply a 2–5% downward correction.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +0.8 → -0.3 → +0.5), model fails to adjust — apply a 3–7% downward bias to forecast mid-horizon.
